title: Which Payments on the Rider Premium Account are Counted Against Arrears
content:
Which of the payments standing on the premium account of one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are counted as money reaching that account follows from the rider's standing.

## The rule

**Where the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium**, every payment posted to the rider premium account is counted, however long ago it was posted.

**Where the rider stands ended**, only the payments posted from the day the rider ended are counted.

**Otherwise**, only the payments posted within the days of grace the rider held allows are counted.

## Condition and result

| The rider's standing | The payments counted |
|---|---|
| Suspended for unpaid premium | Every payment on the account |
| Ended | Those posted from the day the rider ended |
| Any other standing | Those posted within the days of grace the rider held allows |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

A rider premium account carries payments of 30.00 USD, 25.00 USD and 40.00 USD, posted in three successive calendar months up to and including the month of handling, the rider allowing days of grace amounting to a span of 2 whole months.

- **Suspended for unpaid premium:** all three are counted, 95.00 USD.
- **Ended, the rider having ended at the start of the month of handling:** the 40.00 USD posted from that day is counted.
- **Any other standing:** the two posted within the span are counted, 65.00 USD.
